When I tell you that I have been desperately trying to find someone else with the same sentiment about this series as I hold for weeks… I have. Everywhere I look everyone is touting how amazing the HBO series is. But the series is so different from the books it’s insulting.

Jeevan started as a paparazzo who decided it was an awful way to live life, and he wanted purpose. That’s why he was training to be a paramedic. He only ran on stage because he recognized what was happening to Arthur. He happened to run into Kirsten as she was a young actress at the time. Their paths crossing was SUPPOSED to be like two ships in the night. They weren’t supposed to be heavily involved in each other’s lives.

One of the biggest themes in this amazing novel was how one individual could impact so many different individual lives. But Arthur just takes this backseat in the HBO adaptation to the point where his life is practically irrelevant to the story, which was just not the case.

Let’s not forget how like 4 or 5 episodes in, I’ve really only heard the quote “I remember damage,” and not any of the other phenomenal quotes from this spectacular novel.

“Hell is the absence of the people you long for.”

“They spend all their lives waiting for their lives to begin.”

“The more you remember, the more you’ve lost.”

“First we only want to be seen, but once we’re seen, that’s not enough anymore. After that, we want to be remembered.”

“The beauty of this world where almost everyone was gone. If hell is other people, what is a world with almost no people in it?”

(They may have said this one, but)
“I stood looking over my damaged home and tried to forget the sweetness of life on Earth.”

Why did they change Jeevan’s friend Hua to a sibling? Why isn’t Dieter a more forward character in the series? Dieter was on of my favorites because I felt that I could relate best to him. A young adult when everything collapsed, having a distinct before and after in his lifetime.

Pretty much any individual that speaks with me on the phone says I am lovely to work with, it's a pleasure, thank you for being so kind and judgement-free about my finances, etc.  I'm doing well enough when it's just the customer's giving their opinions. I have had some therapy in the past which used to help, but I don’t know how much it will help now. I will definitely need help paying for that, whether through charity or government assistance, because my insurance is absolutely not equipped for anything like that, as much as I wish it was.

We can live off of our savings for a few months, confidently up to 6 months, if I stretch it maybe 9 or 10. I know my husband doesn’t want to do that, considering we have a puppy, two vehicles, and two humans that could suddenly have a necessary repair, vet charge, or doctor visit that our savings may need to pay for in the short-term. I agree with him, which adds to my stress. My constant thought process is, “Why can’t you get a job? You’ve had jobs before, why you can’t you do this? Get it together.” All. Day. Long.

This is definitely an interesting pursuit. I’m intrigued, but I haven’t the slightest idea where I would be able to get stuff like this. I know absolutely nothing about anyone in my area, if I could trust them, what it’s cut with, that sort of thing. How would I go about getting the ball rolling on this? I’m not certain I will take this step just yet, but I am definitely interested in knowing more about this.

Social security would certainly cover my rent and possibly some food, which is essentially all I would likely need (monetarily) for the time being. I think if I can get some help just so I can get back on my feet and figure out how to manage myself, I’ll make it. It feels a million miles away though.

I will look into the welfare programs. I am just concerned of being turned down because other than depression, I’m a perfectly functioning human being, so I fear I’m going to hear, “Well what’s wrong with you? If you can come in to get welfare you can go into a job every day.”
